notes:
I couldn't write any notes on Psalm 149 this time, because I wasn't able to read any of the sources.

The research tool reported that I had no lookups left for this turn. That happened before it returned a single page. I had tried to open the Enduring Word commentary on Psalm 149, the Gill, Ellicott and Pulpit Commentary pages on Bible Hub, Augustine's sermon on the psalm at New Advent, and the Precept Austin page. A second try was blocked the same way. My other tools have no internet access.

You asked me to report only what the pages actually say, so I haven't written notes from memory. Even the verses I'd expect to matter most, such as the "double-edged sword" in vv. 6–9, would be my own recollection rather than what the sources say.

If you send the request again, I'll start with these sources:

1. **Traditional reading:** Enduring Word, plus the Gill, Ellicott and Pulpit Commentary pages on Bible Hub or StudyLight, and Precept Austin. Spurgeon's *Treasury of David* (through Spurgeon.org or StudyLight) is especially relevant to vv. 6–9.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** Wesley's notes (wesley.nnu.edu), Matthew Henry, and searches on Ligonier, Desiring God, Grace to You and the LCMS. This would mainly cover whether the sword in v. 6 should be read literally, as about God's people now, or as about the end times.
3. **Other views:** the NET Bible notes and Bible Odyssey for modern scholarship, and Augustine on New Advent for the Catholic reading. I'd also check whether any of the listed sites discuss popular teaching that applies the psalm to "praise as warfare" or claiming power through praise.

You could also paste the text of those pages here, and I'll write the verse-by-verse notes from them, with a URL for every point.
